investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-23T15:09:58Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the very first network hop to the swarm backend — before any agent identity, VM ID, or state can be returned — all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every contract assertion is unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer received a 502 bad_gateway when attempting POST /api/agents, which proxies to the swarm ELB. Because the failure happens before any agent is provisioned, no evidence can be collected and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is entirely unmet. The identical error message and ~10.9 s latency across all three sibling checks confirms a shared upstream dependency failure rather than an issue in any individual check's logic.

possibleCauses: Primary: The AWS ELB backing the swarm /v1/agents endpoint in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the production-api to return 502 to all callers.

Secondary: A network routing or security-group change between the production-api and the swarm ELB blocked outbound connectivity to the ELB address, producing a connection-refused or timeout that the API layer surfaced as 502.
Tertiary: The swarm service itself (behind the ELB) was restarting, deploying, or had crashed, leaving the ELB with zero healthy instances and returning 502 to the production-api gateway.

Lower probability: A transient DNS resolution failure for the ELB hostname caused the production-api to fail the upstream request; this would also manifest as a 502 but would be expected to self-resolve quickly.

expected-output.contract: contract requires frameTypes to contain generation_completed and imageUrlPresent to equal true — both assertions violated.
